object_description: two offset volumes linked by a semi-buried base
design_condition: The differentiated-height volumes follow the slope, frame tree-lined squares, complete the historic garden wall, and preserve relationships with the castle park and countryside despite their large footprint.

positive.statement: The typological choice of two volumes organized around patios is convincing.
Organizing all elderly psychiatry rooms on a single floor convincingly reflects the Foundation’s demands.
The extended garden wall creates a visual link between the castle complex and the new construction.
The garden is accessible to almost all residents, with rooms oriented toward their surroundings.
The southern common areas benefit from very good sunshine and beautiful perspectives.
The architectural design preserves the valuable trees of the existing park.
The estimated overall cost is in the lower average of the compared projects.

negative.statement: The jury doubts the quality of natural light on the semi-buried ground floor.
The indirect entrance and insufficiently generous hall are not convincing.
The two elevators raise doubts because visitor and logistics flows are not separated.
The jury does not understand the separation glazing between the two living units.
The large footprint produces exterior spaces that are too constructed in character.
The selective connections through the park require deeper reflection on uses.
The extensive glazing makes little use of passive solar strategies and contributes to the project’s poor energy rating.
